title: The Schedule That Finished in 16 Days, Not 12
featured_title: THE SCHEDULE THAT FINISHED IN 16 DAYS NOT 12
subject: civil

presentation.challenge: The shorter branch finished in 12 days, but project completion waited on the longer A-B-D-F path. The correct duration was 16 days.

practice.primary_question: How is project duration determined from activity precedence using the critical path method?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Using the shorter parallel path as the project duration instead of the longest controlling path.

case_dna.target_misconception: When two branches run in parallel, the project duration can be taken from the shorter branch.
case_dna.why_plausible: Parallel work reduces elapsed time, but final completion still waits for the longest predecessor chain.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: A-B-D-F takes 3+5+6+2=16 days, while A-C-E-F takes 3+4+3+2=12 days.
case_dna.corrected_model: Perform a forward pass and use the longest zero-float path as the project duration.

problem_statement: A project has activities: A=3 days; B=5 after A; C=4 after A; D=6 after B; E=3 after C; F=2 after both D and E. Determine project duration, critical path, and total float on the C-E branch.
fixed_constraints: F=2 d after D and E

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The shorter branch was mistaken for the controlling schedule.
facts: F waits for both D and E
gates.prompt: What determines project completion when branches merge?

options.label: Use a forward pass and identify the longest zero-float path
options.reason: The project cannot finish until all required predecessor chains are complete.

options.label: Use the shorter parallel path
options.reason: The merge activity must wait for the longer branch.

options.label: Add every activity duration
options.reason: Parallel activities do not all occur sequentially.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the critical path
gates.hint: The longer path controls the merge into F.

cards.text: The C-E branch has 4 days of total float.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the schedule note
report: C2. F follows both D and E.
C3. Therefore the project duration is 12 days.

claims.label: C1
claims.reason: The shorter path duration is correct.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: F cannot start until the 14-day D branch finishes.

correction.template: Project duration={duration} days; critical path={critical_path}; C-E branch float={float_days} days.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Shorten the project by two days
gates.constraint: Only activity D can be crashed.

options.label: Reduce D from 6 to 4 days
options.reason: The critical path then becomes 14 days, still longer than the 12-day parallel branch.

options.label: Reduce E from 3 to 1 day
options.reason: E is not on the critical path initially.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply CPM again
gates.prompt: If D is reduced to 3 days while all else stays unchanged, what becomes the project duration?

options.label: 12 days
options.reason: A-B-D-F becomes 3+5+3+2=13 days, so 12 days is still too short.

options.label: 13 days
options.reason: A-B-D-F=13 days and A-C-E-F=12 days, so the project duration is 13 days.

gates.explanation: After crashing a critical activity, recompute all paths because the controlling path can change.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the construction schedule
gates.confirmation: I confirm that CPM project duration is controlled by the longest zero-float path through the network.

items.label: What failed
items.value: The shorter parallel branch was treated as project duration.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: The merge activity waits for all predecessors.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use forward/backward passes and identify the zero-float critical path.

seo.seo_title: Critical Path Method Project Duration | FE Civil E-107
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Civil E-107: a construction network with parallel branches finishes in 16 days on critical path A-B-D-F, not 12.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE Civil critical path method project duration
seo.excerpt: Parallel activities do not make the shorter branch control project completion. The longest zero-float path does.
seo.direct_answer: A-B-D-F takes 3+5+6+2=16 days. A-C-E-F takes 12 days, so the project duration is 16 days and the shorter branch has 4 days of float.

faqs.q: What determines project duration in CPM?
faqs.a: The longest zero-float path through the activity network.
